sources.title: Mistral Small 3.1 release announcement
sources.evidence: Dated March 17, 2025; announces Small 3.1, Apache 2.0, text and image capabilities, function calling, 128k context, and separate downloadable Base and Instruct checkpoints.

sources.title: Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct-2503 model card
sources.evidence: Exact instruction-finetuned March 2025 checkpoint; states 24 billion parameters, Apache-2.0, native function calling, text/image understanding and 128k context. Its system-prompt example describes image input and excludes image/audio/video generation or ingestion beyond images. Generic reasoning capability claims do not identify a dedicated thinking mode.

sources.title: Official Small 3.1 model schema and weights rows
sources.evidence: The exact Instruct Weights URL points to Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct-2503 and separately records parameters 24 and active 24. Also specifies Apache 2.0, release 2025-03-17, API identifier mistral-small-2503, text/image input, text output, and function calling. Hosted API retirement is recorded as 2025-11-30.

sources.title: Official weights table renderer and units
sources.evidence: Labels the schema parameters and active columns Parameters (B) and Active (B), establishing billion-parameter units for the separate 24 and 24 values.

sources.title: Exact Instruct checkpoint Transformers configuration
sources.evidence: Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration combines a 40-layer Mistral text model (5120 hidden size, 32 attention heads, 8 KV heads, 32768 MLP size) with a 24-layer Pixtral vision encoder. Text max_position_embeddings is exactly 131072.

sources.title: Exact Instruct checkpoint native Mistral parameters
sources.evidence: Native parameters agree on the 40-layer attention/MLP backbone and 24-layer vision encoder, contain no moe settings, and explicitly set max_position_embeddings to 131072. Retrieved directly over HTTPS after the browser text extractor failed for this file.

sources.title: Mistral native Transformer argument definitions
sources.evidence: TransformerArgs defines moe as optional with default None and explicitly states that setting it switches dense layers to MoE layers; the exact checkpoint native parameters omit that setting.

sources.title: Mistral native Transformer layer implementation
sources.evidence: TransformerBlock uses attention plus FeedForward when moe is None, and constructs routed experts only when moe is supplied. This establishes the dense interpretation of the exact native checkpoint configuration.

name.note: Supported display name for the exact Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct-2503 checkpoint; the frozen ID and alias refer to this instruct release, not its Base checkpoint or Small 3.2.

developer.note: Mistral AI is the first-party developer and publisher; retained catalog display name is Mistral.

family.note: Normalized catalog family follows the explicitly named Mistral Small 3.1 lineage.

release_date.note: Day is explicitly given by the launch announcement and exact model schema; weights and API were announced that day.

open_weights.note: Official announcement links the freely downloadable Instruct checkpoint, and official schema classifies the release Open.

license.note: Apache 2.0 is explicit for the exact Instruct weights.

parameters_b.note: Official nominal total of 24 billion; exact Instruct weights row supplies parameters separately from active. This is not a claim of an independently counted exact 24,000,000,000 tensors.

active_parameters_b.note: Official exact-checkpoint Instruct row explicitly gives Active (B) = 24. Retained as a nominal developer figure, not inferred by equating dense total and active or asserted as a modality-specific per-token tensor census.

architecture.note: Exact native config describes a 40-layer dense attention/MLP text Transformer and a 24-layer vision encoder, without MoE settings; first-party inference definitions select dense FeedForward for this configuration. Transformers config corroborates Mistral plus Pixtral components.

context_window.note: Card advertises 128k; both native params.json and Transformers text config explicitly resolve that checkpoint limit to 131072, not 128000. This is the released checkpoint context, not a claim that a retired hosted endpoint remains available.

modalities.note: Exact model schema lists text/image input and text output, corroborated by multimodal examples and the card system prompt.

reasoning.note: The card claims general reasoning ability but does not establish a dedicated reasoning/thinking mode or its explicit absence for this exact 3.1 checkpoint. Omission from capability enums is insufficient to verify false; Small 3.2 or later model classifications do not transfer. Clear unsupported baseline false.

tool_call.note: Launch, card and model schema explicitly support function calling; card includes native tool-calling setup and examples.

description.value: Instruction-tuned 24B dense multimodal model for text generation, image understanding, and native function calling.
description.note: Replace generic efficiency/extraction wording with directly documented instruction tuning, modalities, architecture and native function calling.

patch.notes: Exact released checkpoint is Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct-2503. Total 24B and active 24B are separately published nominal developer figures in the official weights table, not an exact tensor census or a modality-specific active count. Native and Transformers configuration both resolve the advertised 128k context to 131072 tokens. Dedicated reasoning-mode support remains unverified; generic reasoning benchmarks do not establish it. The hosted mistral-small-2503 API was retired on 2025-11-30; this record describes the released weights.

summary: Confirmed exact March 2025 Instruct identity, release, open weights, modalities and nominal 24B total. Added explicitly published 24B active and Apache-2.0, established dense multimodal Transformer architecture, corrected context from 128000 to 131072 and tool calling from false to true, and replaced the generic description. Clear unsupported reasoning=false to null/unverified; no exact-checkpoint dedicated-mode classification was established.
